what: The CSS Box Shadow Generator lets you design shadows for boxes, cards and buttons with sliders and see them on a live preview. It writes the box-shadow CSS for you, including several layers when you need a more natural look.
Designers and developers use it to get soft card shadows, sharp offset shadows, glows, inner shadows and the soft-plastic neumorphism style without guessing numbers.
It runs in your browser, so nothing is sent anywhere.
uses: Lift a card off the page with a soft shadow that looks natural on light backgrounds.
Add depth to a button, or a stronger shadow for its hover state.
Use Inset to make input fields or pressed buttons look sunken.
Use a bright color with no offset and a large blur for a neon glow.
Combine a dark and a light shadow on a matching background for a soft embossed look.
tutorial: The box in the middle shows your shadow on the chosen background. Open Box and background to change the box color, background color, corner radius and size.
Horizontal offset moves the shadow left or right, vertical offset moves it up or down. Blur makes the edge softer; 0 gives a hard edge.
Spread grows or shrinks the shadow before blurring; negative values keep it tucked under the box. Pick a color and use the opacity slider; most good shadows are only 10 to 30% opaque.
Tick Inset to draw the shadow inside the box instead of outside.
Click Add layer or Duplicate layer, then pick a layer button to edit it. Two or more soft layers look more realistic than one. Remove layer deletes the selected one.
Click a preset to start quickly, then press Copy CSS and paste the box-shadow line into your stylesheet.
features: Stack shadows the way CSS allows, each with its own settings.
Offset X and Y, blur, spread, color, opacity and inset.
See the result on your own box and background colors and corner radius.
Soft, layered, material card, hard offset, glow, inner, neumorphism and floating.
Opaque colors are written as hex and transparent ones as rgba(), one layer per line.

example.title: Worked example: a floating card
example.text: Choose the Layered preset. It creates five shadows with offsets of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 pixels, each 7% black. Together they look like real light falling on paper. Copy CSS gives box-shadow: 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07), … with all five layers. For a hover effect, copy it again after raising the vertical offsets.

tips: Shadows usually fall downward, so use a positive vertical offset and a small or zero horizontal one.
A negative spread with a larger blur gives the soft, modern look many apps use.
On dark backgrounds, shadows are hard to see; a slightly lighter box or a faint glow works better.
Large blur values on many elements can slow down scrolling on old phones; keep heavy shadows for a few key elements.
Match the shadow color to the background hue, for example dark blue instead of black on a blue page, for a richer result.
problems: A parent element probably has overflow: hidden. Add some padding to the parent or remove the overflow rule.
Check the opacity slider, and that the blur and offset are not all 0. On a white box on a white page, increase the opacity.
That style needs the box and background to be the same color. The preset sets both for you.
The Add layer button is grey
The tool allows 10 layers. Remove one first.
